column1: # SUMMARY: Tumors that show evidence of epithelial to mesenchymal transition (EMT) have been associated with metastasis
column3: and poor prognosis. EMT may alter the molecular requirements for growth and survival in different contexts
column4: but the underlying mechanisms remain incomplete. Given the heterogeneity along the EMT spectrum between and within tumors it is important to define the requirements for growth and survival in cells with an epithelial or mesenchymal phenotype to maximize therapeutic efficacy. We have established an inducible cell line model in which a tamoxifen regulatable Twist-ER fusion protein is stably expressed in the H358 non-small cell lung cancer cell line. Upon tamoxifen addition
column5: cells undergo EMT and provide a system in which we can compare the growth and survival requirements directly related to EMT
column6: removing confounding factors present when comparing different cell lines.
